structure: Part 8 read, in full, the three review feature folders under src/server/app/sets/high-risk-plants/journeys/linear/features: check-answers (page.js, controller.js, template.njk, copy.en.js, copy.cy.js, view-model/index.js, view-model/outstanding-parties.js, view-model/rows/change-link.js, summary-row.js, value-text.js, check-answers.fit.spec.js), declaration (page.js, controller.js, template.njk, copy.en.js, copy.cy.js, declaration.fit.spec.js) and confirmation (page.js, controller.js, template.njk, copy.en.js, copy.cy.js, confirmation.fit.spec.js), plus the shared review folder (review/evaluation.js binding the lateness indicator, review/lateness.js computing it) and obligations/sections/review.js (one system obligation, lateNotificationIndicator). For label and number context only it also looked at features/timing-windows.js (2 and 4 days), the arrival-details dateLabels, the place-of-destination headings and kit.CYA_SLUG; those files belong to other parts. Covered: the check your answers page (slug notification-view: three numbered sections, its cards and rows in order, change links, Not provided, outstanding-party and origin errors, the submit section and save actions, the draft late warning, the read-only submitted view with Delete, the late banner, the AMEND Cancel amendment link and success banner); the declaration page (three statements, one checkbox, date of declaration, error, submit flow, lateness stamping, failure handling, submitted redirect); the confirmation page (panel and reference, body, date, late banner, two links, no back link, draft redirect); the lateness rules; the review obligation; and every test in the three fit specs (3 + 4 + 2 = 9). It stops at the dashboard the confirmation links to.

claims.statement: A potato notification is late when today (UK time) is after the day 2 days before the arrival date.
claims.quote:
const deadline = addUtcDays(
    arrivalDay,
    potato ? -POTATO_DAYS_BEFORE_ARRIVAL : PLANTS_WOOD_DAYS_AFTER_ARRIVAL
  )
  return startOfDayInZone(clock, 'Europe/London') > deadline
    ? 'late'
    : 'on-time'
claims.note: So notifying exactly 2 days before arrival is on time; 1 day before or on the day is late. The fit spec's late case uses an arrival date of today.
